anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: The old man crucified with Christ.
If we died with him, we shall also live with him.
Quoted: I live no longer I; Christ lives in me.

choices.why: Paul speaks of himself without covering.

pass_a_gloss: For that the perfect has a beginning of another birth and becomes another than what he was, the apostle teaches us, saying sometimes: The old man was crucified with Christ, and again: If we died with him we shall also live with him, and about himself plainly: I live no longer I, but Christ lives in me.
pass_b_english: For that the perfect has a beginning of another birth and becomes another than what he was, the apostle teaches us. At one time he says: "The old man was crucified with Christ" (Romans 6:6); and again: "If we died with him, we shall also live with him." (2 Timothy 2:11) And of himself he says plainly: "I live no longer I, but Christ lives in me." (Galatians 2:20) (Romans 6:8)
